I need help concerning sewing machines - Instruction/selection

Some fabric shops have a bunch of machines that you can try out with guidance of the employees.

Don't buy one that has 100 decorative seems/programs you wont need it and it will jack up the price. Brother and singer are two good brands. Opt for a machine in the 200-300 dollar category with a strong motor, sometimes called jeans sewing machines.

Check out community collage, community centers and shops to find courses in sewing.
That was like another Christmas Present! Thanks, Vivala!

Sumguy is right about the repairshops aswell.

What you need as a beginner from a machine is one that is easy to thread and wont fuss around if yo manhandle it a bit, hence the strong motor/jeans machine option. When you sew on the machine you will most likely only use 3 different seams. The straight line, zig-zag so the edges of the fabric don't rip and/or the 3-step zig-zag for stretchier fabric around the edges and/or baby clothing/underwear.

All basic machines have these seams so thats nothing you need to worry about. Make sure you try them out and find one that suits you ergonomically and is easy to thread/a reliable brand/machine.

I did a ton of research last year about this (more for general sewing than quilting, there May be some differences) and found that Janome has one machine that's considered the best of the best for new sewers, and is produced and sold under 3~4 other brand names too (like Baby Lock). Of course I can't remember the model and my wife decided that ~$250 was too much so she put an $80 Brother in her Amazon wish list and received that for Christmas.

Beyond that the overwhelming majority of recommendations were to visit a sewing machine repair place and buy from them, from their stock on hand. Used machines so you'll be paying less than new, but fully serviced and with a guarantee. The machines are often trade-ins as people decide they want a new feature and trade up, plus they will help guide you to the best machine for you and keep you away from machines that need a lot of service work (some brands or models). Unfortunately I live rural and a 3~4 hour round trip drive just for something sewing related isn't in the cards for me, but you might be in a different situation.
